Axle Energy brief, made with Ryan Hennebry’s competitor-intel agent

On 24 September, the agent read 179 pages on Axle, Voltalis, ev.energy, Enode, gridX, Kaluza and Kraken, logging 248 claims.

  1. Quick take
  2. Recommendations
  3. Where each rival is moving
  4. Who trades, and who pays
  5. Open questions
  6. Also built by Ryan

Quick take

Voltalis’ installers will decide which French homes Axle’s partners can sell into. Its French FAQ says a home can be operated by only one flexibility operator at a time.Voltalis FAQvoltalis.com · read 24 Sep 2026Paraphrased from French: A home can be operated by only one flexibility operator at a time.1 It plans 150 more installers by the end of 2026, fitting free thermostats in the French government’s 109 priority territories.Voltalis installer releasegroup.voltalis.com · 14 Sep 2026Paraphrased from French: Voltalis plans 150 more installer technicians by the end of the year.2

Axle’s French partner segments should be ones Voltalis’ free home thermostats do not reach. Commercial and industrial sites, where SolarEdge starts with Axle before residential batteries, sit outside a household thermostat programme.Axle’s SolarEdge postaxle.energy · 18 Aug 2026“SolarEdge is now launching with Axle as its first flexibility partner in France”3

Voltalis already sells the market side in France. It says it trades on every French market since its aFRR certification of 2 July 2026, and that it raised €91M in 2023.Voltalis aFRR releasegroup.voltalis.com · 2 Jul 2026Paraphrased from French: Voltalis says it is now present on all French electricity markets: FCR, aFRR and mFRR reserves, day-ahead, intraday and the Capacity Mechanism.Voltalis group pagegroup.voltalis.com · read 24 Sep 2026“Voltalis secures €91M to speed up its expansion”4,5 So a French maker Axle pitches may find its customers already in homes Voltalis operates.

Recommendations

After SolarEdge’s commercial sites, sign more French homes Voltalis’ thermostats do not reach. Voltalis states about 300,000 buildings connected.Voltalis aFRR releasegroup.voltalis.com · 2 Jul 2026Paraphrased from French: Voltalis counts 300,000 buildings and 1.5 million connected appliances.4 Its 150 installers are still a plan, not homes fitted.Voltalis installer releasegroup.voltalis.com · 14 Sep 2026Paraphrased from French: Voltalis plans 150 more installer technicians by the end of the year.2 Next step: ask RTE whether the one-operator rule is its own before signing French homes.

Each GB partner’s next country is where Kaluza’s new maker offer meets Axle. Kaluza’s Flex for OEMs, 2 April 2026, offers makers markets “without requiring in-house trading expertise”, and its homepage shows myenergi and Hypervolt logos.Kaluza Flex for OEMs postkaluza.com · 2 Apr 2026“Aggregation and orchestration enables participation in capacity, wholesale and local flexibility markets without requiring in-house trading expertise.”Kaluza homepagekaluza.com · read 24 Sep 2026Paraphrased: Hypervolt and myenergi appear on both Axle’s and Kaluza’s homepage logo strips.18,19 Next step: sign each GB partner’s next market before Kaluza’s offer names one.

Kraken is wired to carmakers, Renault included, but its flexibility sales role names none as buyers, and its Generation Flexibility product is not listed as live in France. Its Jedlix purchase, 21 October 2024, brought “API integration agreements” with makers including Renault, Polestar, Kia and Hyundai.Kraken’s Jedlix releasekraken.tech · 21 Oct 2024“The company brings an international catalogue of API integration agreements with EV and charger manufacturers and energy companies including Renault, Polestar, Kia, Hyundai, Engie, Eneco, Vattenfall, EDF Luminus, Wien Energie, CKW, Next Energy, Yve, Easee, Zaptec, Go-E, Wallbox, and more.”17 Its flexibility sales role names “utilities, retailers, aggregators, grid operators, IPPs and asset owners”, and the live countries on its Generation Flexibility page leave out France.Kraken sales director postapi.ashbyhq.com · read 24 Sep 2026“You’ll lead enterprise sales across the flexibility ecosystem, working with utilities, retailers, aggregators, grid operators, IPPs and asset owners to bring Kraken’s flexibility platform to market.”Kraken Generation Flexibilitykraken.tech · read 24 Sep 2026Paraphrased: Kraken’s Generation Flexibility page lists where it is live: the Netherlands, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United Kingdom. France is not among them.20,21 Next step: pitch Renault, a French carmaker, the grid payout Kraken leaves to utilities.

Open questions

  1. Is one operator per home an RTE rule or a Voltalis term? RTE’s NEBEF page does not carry it.RTE NEBEF listservices-rte.com · read 24 Sep 2026Paraphrased: RTE lists Voltalis, under its own code, as the one operator qualified for its NEBEF sub-metering experiment. The list covers that experiment alone.11 If it is RTE’s, homes Axle signs first are shut to Voltalis too.
  2. Which markets does Kaluza’s ENGIE licence cover? Announced from London and Paris on 25 September 2025, it names none.Kaluza and ENGIE releasekaluza.com · 25 Sep 2025Paraphrased: Kaluza signed a multi-year licensing agreement with ENGIE across several markets, announced from London and Paris. The markets are not named.32
